title: Multiplayer Water Cycle Visualization
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D water cycle visualization using Three.js where multiple 'players' (simulated via colored cursors) can interact with different stages of the water cycle simultaneously.

SCENE SETUP:
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 15, 30), looking at origin, FOV 60
- Lights: DirectionalLight (intensity 1.0) at (10, 20, 10), AmbientLight (intensity 0.4)
- Background: Gradient sky using a large sphere with shader material (light blue at top, white at horizon)
- Ground: A terrain mesh (PlaneGeometry 40x40, segments 20x20) with vertex displacement to create hills and a valley. Color it green/brown.
- Ocean: A flat blue semi-transparent plane (20x10) at y=0.2 on the right side of the scene
- Sun: A bright yellow sphere (radius 2) at position (15, 18, -5) with a PointLight
- Mountain: A cone geometry (radius 4, height 10) at position (-10, 5, 0), colored grey/white at peak
- Clouds: 3 cloud groups at positions (-5,12,0), (5,13,2), (0,14,-3), each made of merged sphere geometries, white material

WATER CYCLE STAGES & PARTICLES:
- Implement a particle system using BufferGeometry with 500 small spheres (or point sprites) representing water molecules
- Each particle has a 'phase' property: 'liquid' (blue), 'vapor' (white/transparent), 'ice' (light cyan), 'rain' (dark blue)
- Particles cycle through stages:
  1. EVAPORATION: Liquid particles near ocean/ground rise upward when heated (speed 0.02-0.05 units/frame), turning to vapor
  2. CONDENSATION: Vapor particles near cloud altitude (y>10) slow down and cluster near clouds, becoming visible
  3. PRECIPITATION: When a cloud accumulates >30 particles, it starts raining - particles fall as rain (speed -0.08 units/frame)
  4. COLLECTION: Rain particles hitting ground flow toward ocean (x velocity toward ocean), becoming liquid again
  5. FREEZING: Rain particles hitting the mountain above y>7 turn to ice (cyan) and slide down slowly

MULTIPLAYER SYSTEM:
- Support 2 players, toggled via Tab key
- Player 1 (Red cursor): Controls the Sun - click and drag to move sun position, affecting evaporation rate
- Player 2 (Blue cursor): Controls Wind - click and drag to set wind direction vector, affecting cloud/vapor movement
- Display current player indicator in top-left corner as a colored circle + text
- Each player has a 'score' representing how many particles they've influenced

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Tab: Switch active player (cycles Player1 -> Player2 -> Player1)
- Click + Drag on scene: Player 1 moves sun (constrained to y>5, x/z within [-20,20]); Player 2 sets wind vector
- Press 'H' to toggle heat boost (doubles evaporation rate for Player 1's sun)
- Press 'W' to toggle wind boost (doubles wind strength for Player 2)
- Press 'R' to reset all particles to initial liquid state in ocean
- Press 'C' to manually trigger condensation burst (all vapor instantly condenses)
- Press 'F' to toggle freeze mode (all precipitation becomes ice)
- Press 'Space' to pause/resume the simulation

HUD/UI ELEMENTS:
- Top-left: Active player indicator (div#player-indicator)
- Top-right: Statistics panel (div#stats-panel) showing:
  - Liquid count, Vapor count, Rain count, Ice count
  - Evaporation rate (particles/sec)
  - Current temperature (derived from sun proximity, range 0-100)
  - Wind speed (0-10 scale)
  - Cycle completions (how many full liquid->vapor->rain->liquid cycles completed)
- Bottom: Phase diagram bar (div#phase-bar) showing proportional colored segments for each phase
- Center-bottom: Simulation speed indicator

STATE MANAGEMENT - window.__3D_STATE__ must expose:
{
  activePlayer: 1 or 2,
  sunPosition: {x, y, z},
  windVector: {x, y, z},
  particleCounts: {liquid: N, vapor: N, rain: N, ice: N},
  totalParticles: 500,
  evaporationRate: Number (particles per second),
  temperature: Number (0-100),
  windSpeed: Number (0-10),
  cycleCompletions: Number,
  isPaused: false,
  heatBoost: false,
  windBoost: false,
  freezeMode: false,
  player1Score: Number,
  player2Score: Number,
  simulationTime: Number (seconds elapsed),
  cloudParticleCounts: [N, N, N] (per cloud)
}

PHYSICS:
- Evaporation rate = baseRate * (temperature / 50) * (heatBoost ? 2 : 1)
- Temperature = clamp(100 - distance(sun, ocean) * 3, 0, 100)
- Wind affects all vapor/rain particles: particle.velocity += windVector * 0.01 * (windBoost ? 2 : 1)
- Gravity on rain: -0.08 units/frame
- Particle positions must stay within bounds: x[-20,20], y[0,20], z[-15,15]
- Conservation: totalParticles must always equal sum of all phase counts (500)

ANIMATION:
- Clouds slowly bob up/down (sin wave, amplitude 0.3, period 4 seconds)
- Ocean surface has gentle wave animation (vertex displacement)
- Sun has a subtle pulsing glow effect
- Particles have size variation based on phase (vapor=small, rain=medium, ice=large, liquid=medium)
- Rain particles leave brief trail effect
physics_constraints: Particle conservation: sum of all phase counts must always equal 500. Temperature derived from sun-ocean distance: T = clamp(100 - dist*3, 0, 100). Evaporation rate scales with temperature. Gravity = -0.08 per frame on rain. All particle positions bounded within [-20,20] x [0,20] x [-15,15]. Wind force applied as velocity increment. Cloud precipitation threshold: 30 particles.
